newsitem.title: USA: Decent demand seen for U.S. Treasury 10-yr notes.
newsitem.headline: Decent demand seen for U.S. Treasury 10-yr notes.

text.p: After a somewhat disappointing three-year note auction Tuesday, market participants have higher hopes for Wednesday's 10-year note sale.
The Treasury is slated to sell $10 billion in 10-year notes at 1300 EST/1800 GMT. Players expect the average yield to come in at anywhere from 6.26 percent to 6.30 percent.

"I think it'll be a relatively good auction given where yields have gone," said Marilyn Schaja, money market economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. "According to our traders, this ought to go better than the 30-year."
The when-issued 10-year note was at 6.26 percent.

Demand should be good for the issue, traders said. "Essentially, all high profile players are inclined to like this issue," said one trader at a primary dealership, adding that mortgage guys and foreign accounts want it.
Some noted that the 10-year is a benchmark in many other countries, along with the 30-year the bellwether in the U.S. The Treasury sells $10 billion 30-year bonds Thursday.
Meanwhile, the three-year notes sold Tuesday have performed well, players pointed out.
The three-year "came, it went and it's trading at a profit. What else to do you want?," wondered a trader.
Michael Norman, publisher of the Economic Contrarian Update, said that while the auction won't go as well as if yields were higher, the "economic environment is still very positive for bonds."

Getting through supply may be difficult because of the lower yields, he said. And, "we've probably seen the best from the budget (deficit) side for quite some time." Norman said. "They'll be concerns about supply as we see the deficit expanding again."
